description: The PROP-19/CRIT-103 textual contradiction flagged in the prior round IS now genuinely resolved at the spec/contract layer: specs/verification-architecture.md:41 (PROP-19 row) now explicitly states the three-state precedence and says verbatim 'State (a)'s "never boilerplate" guarantee is therefore scoped to the case a real draft path IS supplied, not an unconditional guarantee across all three states' -- this matches contracts/sprint-2.md:15-17 (CRIT-103) exactly, and the REQ-4b distinction (state (b) is a caller-shape-only wiring safety-net, never reached from the real REQ-19 daily-executor invocation, which per specs/behavioral-spec.md:93-95's 'research -> write -> V0/V0.5 -> post' single-session flow always supplies topic/research and the authored draft together) is logically coherent. HOWEVER, this fix was applied ONLY at the spec/contract prose layer and was NOT propagated to the actual implementation artifacts that CRIT-103's own passThreshold designates as the proof surface, so the exact same 'unconditional never boilerplate' contradiction the round-2 pass flagged now lives on, verbatim, one layer down, in the real code and its own test file: (1) skills/profitable-article-writer/run.sh:120's comment says the boilerplate heredoc (lines 124-140) is 'reserved for ARTICLE_TEST=1 hermetic tests only' -- but the 'if' guard at run.sh:116 that gates the real-content copy is FALSE whenever ARTICLE_TEST=1 is unset AND ARTICLE_REAL_DRAFT_PATH is empty/missing, meaning the SAME boilerplate heredoc the comment calls ARTICLE_TEST=1-only is directly, unconditionally reachable in real (non-ARTICLE_TEST) mode -- exactly PROP-19's now-corrected state (b). (2) skills/profitable-article-writer/tests/test-prop19-real-content-hook.sh:2-4's own header comment says, unconditionally, run.sh's 'REAL (non-ARTICLE_TEST) generate_draft hook uses the running agent's OWN real research+craft content ... VERBATIM, never the ARTICLE_TEST=1 boilerplate template' -- yet the SAME file's own section (b) (lines 30-38) explicitly drives run.sh in real (non-ARTICLE_TEST) mode with topic+research set and no draft path, and asserts the boilerplate marker IS present in the output (test-prop19-real-content-hook.sh:38: 'falls back to the boilerplate template'). This is a direct, self-contained contradiction between a file's own header claim and its own test body -- the identical failure pattern (an unconditional 'never boilerplate' claim falsified by a documented, tested fallback state) that this contract-review round was supposed to have eliminated, now surfacing in the implementation/test artifacts CRIT-103 cites as its proof (tests/test-prop19-real-content-hook.sh) rather than in the spec prose. CRIT-103 therefore does NOT cleanly trace to a non-contradicted state of the WHOLE artifact chain (spec -> contract -> code/test): the spec and contract are now internally consistent with each other, but the code and its own test file that will actually be graded in Phase 3 still assert the pre-correction, falsified claim about their own behavior.
